:::{#thm-substitution-logic}
#### Replacing a part by an equivalent part

Let $A$ and $B$ be [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent) [propositions](#def-proposition).
Replacing $A$ by $B$ inside a larger [proposition](#def-proposition)
gives a proposition logically equivalent to the larger one.
In particular, $\neg A \equiv \neg B$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

Whether the larger [proposition](#def-proposition) is true in a row of its [truth table](#def-truth-table)
depends only on whether $A$ is true in that row, not on how $A$ is written.
$A$ and $B$ are true in the same rows,
so the two larger [propositions](#def-proposition) are true in the same rows too.

:::

:::
